claims.binder: (hf : MDifferentiableAt I I' f ((extChartAt I α).symm z))
claims.reason:
I checked the argument and it holds. Let x := (extChartAt I α).symm z. By `inChartAt_apply` and `mpullback_apply`, the left side at v is ω (f x) (fun i ↦ mfderiv I I' f x (mfderivWithin 𝓘(ℝ,E) I (extChartAt I α).symm (range I) z (v i))). The right side at v is ω (f x) (fun i ↦ mfderivWithin … (f ∘ (extChartAt I α).symm) (range I) z (v i)).

Case 1: f is differentiable at x. The existing proof applies unchanged.

Case 2: f is not differentiable at x. Then `mfderiv_zero_of_not_mdifferentiableAt` (Mathlib MFDeriv/Basic.lean:523) gives mfderiv f x = 0, so the left side is ω (f x) (fun _ ↦ 0). Suppose g := f ∘ (extChartAt I α).symm were MDifferentiableWithinAt (range I) z.
- The point x lies in (chartAt H α).source: this follows from `(extChartAt I α).map_target hz` and `extChartAt_source`, as at line 83 of the same file.
- `mdifferentiableAt_extChartAt` (Atlas.lean:345, which uses the `[IsManifold I 1 M]` still in scope) makes extChartAt I α MDifferentiableAt x.
- extChartAt I α x = z by right_inv, and extChartAt maps every point into range I.
- So `MDifferentiableWithinAt.comp` (Basic.lean:1154) with s = univ, u = range I, together with `mdifferentiableWithinAt_univ`, makes g ∘ extChartAt I α differentiable at x.
- On the open set (chartAt H α).source, which contains x, g ∘ extChartAt I α equals f by left_inv. `MDifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq` (Basic.lean:1032) would then make f differentiable at x, a contradiction.
Hence `mfderivWithin_zero_of_not_mdifferentiableWithinAt` (Basic.lean:519) gives mfderivWithin g = 0, and the right side is also ω (f x) (fun _ ↦ 0).

The two sides agree in both cases. hf appears nowhere else in the statement, so deleting it leaves a statement that elaborates. All cited lemmas exist with the stated hypotheses.
